## Setup

### Packages

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# Packages to use
# tidyverse includes ggplot2
# janitor and DataExplorer are good for data wrangling 
packages = c("tidyverse", "janitor", "DataExplorer", "ggtext")

packageCheck = function(x) {
    if (!require(x, character.only = TRUE)) {
      install.packages(x, dependencies = TRUE)
      library(x, character.only = TRUE)
    }
  }

# Now load or install & load all
loadPacks<-lapply(packages, packageCheck)
set.seed(10)
```

## Data Wrangling

### Clean covariate data

Covariate data includes metadata in values spaces that needs to be removed. Some column names can be shortened for clarity and concision.

```{r}
cleanCovar <- covar %>%
  separate(col="mat_age_yrs", into = c(NA, "mat_age"), sep = "\\ ", 
           convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="preg_preeclampsia", into = c(NA, "preg_preeclampsia"), 
           sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="delivery_gestAge_wks", into = c(NA, "delivery_weeks"), 
           sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="sampleCollection_gestAge_wks", into = c(NA, "sample_weeks"), 
           sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="batch_Microarray", into = c(NA, "batch_Microarray"), 
           sep = "\\ ", convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="mat_BMI", into = c(NA, "mat_BMI"), sep = "\\ ", 
           convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="mat_vitD", into = c(NA, "mat_vitD"), sep = "\\ ", 
           convert = TRUE) %>%
  separate(col="mat_asthma", into = c(NA, "mat_asthma"), sep = "\\ ", 
           convert = TRUE)
```

### Add gene names to gene expression data

```{r}
named_genes <- geneExp %>%
  rename(PROBEID = X) %>%
  left_join(geneNames, by = "PROBEID")
```

### Pivot named genes into a long data frame

```{r}
long_genes <- named_genes %>%
  pivot_longer(col = c(starts_with("GSM")), values_to = "geneExp", 
               names_to = "geoID")
```

### Join covariate data and gene expression data

```{r}
long_cov_genes <- long_genes %>%
  left_join(cleanCovar, by = "geoID")
```

### Turn two categorical covariates into factors

```{r}
# Preeclampsia status
long_cov_genes$preg_preeclampsia <- factor(long_cov_genes$preg_preeclampsia)

# Maternal asthma status
long_cov_genes$mat_asthma <- factor(ifelse(long_cov_genes$mat_asthma == 1, 
                                           "Asthma", "Not Asthma"))
```

### Turn one continuous covariate into a categorical covariate
Remember to include this information in labels
```{r}
# Delivery weeks in buckets
# Very Early: before 36 weeks
# Early: between 36 and 38 weeks
# On time: between 38 and 40 weeks
# Late: after 40 weeks

long_cov_genes$delivery_time <- factor(
  ifelse(long_cov_genes$delivery_weeks < 36, "Very Early", 
         ifelse(long_cov_genes$delivery_weeks < 38, "Early", 
                ifelse(long_cov_genes$delivery_weeks > 40, "Late", "On Time"))), 
  levels = c("Very Early", "Early", "On Time", "Late"), ordered = TRUE)
levels(long_cov_genes$delivery_time)
summary(long_cov_genes$delivery_time)
```

### Histogram Function
```{r}
# Histogram
create_histogram <- function(df, geneName){
  # x is gene expression 
  ggplot(df, aes(x = geneExp)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 40) + 
    labs(
      title = paste0(geneName," Gene Expression in Subset of VDAART Study"),
      x = paste0("Gene Expression of ", geneName),
      y = "Frequency" # find units 
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_textbox_simple(
        padding = margin(t = 10, b = 10)
      )
    )
}
```

### Scatterplot Function

```{r}
create_scatterplot <- function(df, geneName, contCov){
  # x is continuous covariate, y is gene expression
  # covariate currently hard coded 
  ggplot(df, aes(x = mat_vitD, y = geneExp)) + 
    geom_point() +
    labs(
      title = paste0("Maternal Vitamin D vs. Gene Expression of ", geneName,
                     " at Trial Entry (10-18 Weeks Gestation)"),
      x = "Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)", # contCov
      y = paste0("Expression of ", geneName) # geneName 
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_textbox_simple(
        padding = margin(t = 10, b = 10)
      )
    )
}
```

### Boxplot Function
add jitter!
```{r}
create_boxplot <- function(df, geneName, catCov1, catCov2){
  # y is gene expression, x is delivery time in buckets, 
  # color is preeclampsia status
  # preeclampsia and delivery time currently hard coded
  boxplot <- ggplot(df, aes(x = delivery_time, y = geneExp, 
                        color = preg_preeclampsia)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) +
    labs(
      y = geneName,
      x = "Pregnancy Duration in Weeks",
      color = "Preeclampsia Status", 
      title = paste0("Gene Expression of ", geneName, 
                     " with Pregnancy Duration and Preeclampsia Status")
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    scale_x_discrete(
      name = "Pregnancy Duration in Weeks",
      labels = c("< 36", "36-38", "38-40", "> 40")
    ) +
    scale_color_discrete(
      name = "Preeclampsia Status",
      labels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")
    ) +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge()) +
    #geom_jitter(width = 0.2) + 
    theme(
      plot.title = element_textbox_simple(
        padding = margin(t = 10, b = 10)
      )
    )

  return(boxplot)
}
```

## Define function to create all three plots for a given gene

```{r}
create_plot <- function(df, geneName, contCov, catCov1, catCov2){
  # get only relevant parts of the dataframe 
  gene <- df[which(df["GENE"] == geneName),]
  # save plots to vector to be returned as one object 
  plots <- c()
  
  # still passing geneName separately so it's easier to get for titles and labels

  plots <- append(plots, create_histogram(gene, geneName))
  plots <- append(plots, create_scatterplot(gene, geneName, contCov))
  plots <- append(plots, create_boxplot(gene, geneName, catCov1, catCov2))
  return(plots)
}
```

## Define function to iterate over list of genes

```{r}
# function to create all of three plots for each gene name given
create_plots <- function(df, geneNames, contCov = "mat_vitD", 
                         catCov1 = "delivery_time", 
                         catCov2 = "preg_preeclampsia"){
  # save plots to vector to be returned as one object 
  emptyPlots <- c()

  # iterate over list of genes
  for (i in geneNames) {
    # create all three types of plots for each gene 
    emptyPlots <- append(emptyPlots, create_plot(df, i, contCov, catCov1, catCov2))
  }
  
  return(emptyPlots)
}
```

## Call function to produce plots
Genes chosen:
RASAL3 plays a role in signalling and T cell regulation. It is associated with diverticulitis and epiphyseal dysplasia.

```{r}
# List of genes to examine

allPlots <- create_plots(df = long_cov_genes, geneNames = geneNames, 
                         contCov = "mat_vitD", catCov1 = "delivery_time", 
                         catCov2 = "preg_preeclampsia")

# Show plots
allPlots
```
